content.user_title: Assess Web Vulnerabilities with a Top 100 Reference
content.value_statement: Teams need consistent language for common web security flaws. This skill provides a structured OWASP-aligned reference with causes, impacts, and mitigations.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes 100 web vulnerability types across 15 categories.
Explains definitions, root causes, impacts, and mitigations for common flaws.
Maps listed vulnerabilities to OWASP Top 10 2021 categories.
Provides quick-reference tables for key controls and security headers.
Covers APIs, authentication, access control, SSRF, mobile, IoT, and business logic flaws.
limitations: It is a reference guide, not an automated scanner.
It does not verify live systems or run security tools.
It does not replace legal authorization or professional penetration testing.
It may not include the newest CVEs or framework-specific guidance.

use_cases.title: Build Assessment Checklists
use_cases.description: Create structured review checklists from the vulnerability categories, impacts, and control guidance.

use_cases.title: Plan Secure Fixes
use_cases.description: Match a suspected flaw to likely root causes and practical mitigation patterns.

use_cases.title: Standardize Review Language
use_cases.description: Use shared terminology for security reviews, remediation planning, and training materials.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Vulnerability Category
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the authentication vulnerabilities in this reference. Include root causes, likely impacts, and common mitigations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Review Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a concise checklist for reviewing access control issues in a web application using this reference.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Finding to Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Map this finding to the closest vulnerability type in the reference and suggest practical controls: [describe finding].

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize a Security Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Group these application risks by category, likely business impact, and remediation priority using the reference: [paste risk list].

output_examples.input: Explain SSRF risk for an image URL feature.
output_examples.output: SSRF occurs when a server fetches user-controlled URLs without validation. Key controls include allowlists, egress filtering, and blocked metadata endpoints.

output_examples.input: Create a checklist for API key exposure.
output: Check repositories and client bundles for exposed keys.
Confirm keys are stored in managed secret storage.
Verify rotation, least privilege, and monitoring are enabled.

output_examples.input: Map missing authorization on document access.
output_examples.output: This aligns with IDOR and broken access control. The likely root cause is missing object-level authorization on each request.

best_practices: Use the reference to classify risks before writing remediation tasks.
Pair each vulnerability type with concrete evidence from the reviewed system.
Validate mitigations against the application architecture and threat model.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the list as proof that a system is vulnerable.
Do not run security tests without clear authorization.
Do not replace current vendor advisories with this static reference.

faq.question: Does this skill scan applications?
faq.answer: No. It provides reference guidance for understanding and organizing web vulnerability analysis.

faq.question: Is the reference aligned with OWASP?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an OWASP Top 10 2021 mapping and related vulnerability categories.

faq.question: Can developers use it for remediation?
faq.answer: Yes. Each vulnerability entry includes root causes, impacts, and mitigation guidance.

faq.question: Can it replace a penetration test?
faq.answer: No. It supports analysis and planning, but it does not perform testing or validate live systems.

faq.question: Does it include API security topics?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers insecure endpoints, exposed API keys, rate limiting, and related API risks.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
